Concept of History and its Importance

History is the study of past. The word "history" is derived from the Greek word "historia" which means seeking knowledge through inquiry, narratives and historical records. History is much more than simply describing and learning the rise and fall of empires and nations. History is fascinating because it investigates patterns of human behaviour found in different cultures and civilizations around the world.
Concept of History and its Importance
The footprints of human history inform us how different experiences and events in the past have shaped our present world, providing us with a picture of where we stand today.
Quote
"History never looks like history when you are living through it." — John W Gardner (1912-2002 United States)
Footprints of Human History

Period | Dates; Stone Age | 35000 BC to 4000 BC; Bronze Age | 3500 BC to 1200 BC; Ancient Egypt | 3100 BC to 332 BC; Indus Valley Civilization | 2500 BC to 1500 BC; Early Islamic Civilization | 570 AD to 750 AD; American Revolution | 1775 AD to 1783 AD; The French Revolution | 1789 AD to 1799 AD; World War 2 | 1939 AD to 1945 AD; The Moon Landing | 1969 AD
Note for Teachers

Divide the class in groups and instruct them to carefully examine the Picture "Footprints of Human History". Ask the students to discuss the impacts of some historical developments and inventions in human history. Students can make a list of the impacts to share with the class. Make sure you understand facts accurately.
Why Study History?

The importance of studying history is manifold. Historical records help us in understanding the root causes of the problems and enable us to make informed decisions in the future. In this regard, international organizations such as the United Nations serve as a forum for international cooperation in the development and preservation of global peace and security.
Do You Know?
There are five main organs of the United Nations; the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the Secretariat, and the International Court of Justice.
How to Learn About the Past

History is a tool for understanding the past and the present. Historians are like detectives. As detectives use clues to solve mysteries, historians also use clues as sources to examine and interpret the past. These historical sources are classified into two types: primary sources and secondary sources. Primary sources include letters, diaries, court records, photographs and interviews.
How to Learn About the Past
On the other hand, secondary sources provide analysis on primary sources. Good examples of secondary sources include dictionaries, encyclopaedias, books, and journal articles.
Note for Teachers
Examine some contributions of the United Nations to the global peace. The teacher can discuss with the students some examples of past disputes that were settled by the United Nations.
Recording an Oral History
Interview an elderly relative about a historical event that happened in his or her lifetime. During the interview, take notes on what you learned about the event.
Do you Know the principles of studying history?
Interpret and explain historical sources/evidences by being objective and unbiased. • Analyze and evaluate the sources critically. • Draw conclusions from the information logically.
Do You Know?
Artefacts: Investigating artefacts such as utensils, tools, clothing, and coins can teach us about past behaviour and community activities.
Do You Know?
Written records: Provide interpretations of past events by the historians.
Pre-History

The term Pre-History was introduced in English by archaeologist Daniel Wilson in 1851. This term is used to indicate the period of history in which there are no written or concrete record of past. More broadly, it refers to all the time preceding human existence till the invention of writing. It includes the stone age and the metal age.
Stone Age
The Stone Age is a vast era in pre-history during which early humans started using stones, such as flint, to make tools and weapons. It is the earliest known period of human culture.
Stone Age
The stone age can be further classified in to three phases:
Stone Age
The Paleolithic period (old Stone Age) • The Mesolithic period (middle Stone Age) • The Neolithic period (late Stone Age)
Metal Age

During the Metal Age people started using metals, such as copper, tin, bronze and iron, to make tools and weapons. That's why this age is called metal age. The Metal Age began about 6,000 years ago. The metal age can be also classified into three phases:
Metal Age
The Copper Age • The Bronze Age • The Iron Age.
Ancient Civilizations of the World

Understanding modern world history requires knowledge of ancient and medieval history. Ancient civilization refers to the first settled societies that served as the foundation of future states, nations, and empires. The term civilization is derived from the Latin word "civis" which means "someone who lives in a city or town" or "a citizen or a city dweller".
Ancient Civilizations of the World

Civilization is the most advanced stage of a society's social and cultural development. Historians define civilization as a complex society with five characteristics: (i) organized cities, (ii) specialised workers, (iii) complex institutions, (iv) writing system and record keeping, and (v) advanced technology. The map depicts the geographic locations of the early civilizations i.e.
Ancient Civilizations of the World
Indus Valley, Mesopotamia, Egypt, the Shang and Zhou dynasties of ancient China.
Note for Teachers
Describe the location of Mesopotamia and other civilizations mentioned on the Map.
Facts to Know

Inform the students that historians outline some basic features that were common in the early civilizations. These features are: (i) agriculture (ii) town planning (iii) well-organized government (iv) complex religions (v) job specialization (vi) arts and architecture (vii) public works and (viii) writing. Examples can be quoted from the past.
Early River Valley Civilizations

The world's early civilizations such as Mesopotmia, Egypt, Indus valley and China developed along the banks of warm rivers. The rivers provided people with a continuous source of water and fertile soil for domestic use and agricultural activities such as farming, livestock, and fishing. Agriculture and domestication of animals were important features of all civilizations.
Early River Valley Civilizations
Water tanks, dykes, and small dams were built near river banks to store water for irrigation of farmlands through water channels.
Mesopotamian Civilizations

The word Mesopotamia comes from Greek word meaning "land between the rivers", the Tigris and Euphrates. Lower Mesopotamia is located in modern-day Iraq. Whereas Upper Mesopotamia is located in Syria and Turkey that forms the Fertile Crescent; a
Note for Teachers
Ask the students to identify and label features/characteristics of the River Valley civilization depicted in the photograph.
Mesopotamian Civilizations

crescent-shaped area of land in the Middle East, with flat mud plains and fertile soil. Some of the major Mesopotamian civilizations, as shown on the map, include Sumerian, Assyrian, Akkadian, and Babylonian civilizations.
Facts to Know

Fertile Crescent was unique among ancient civilizations. It was regarded as the place of origin of agriculture, urbanization, writing, trade, science, history, and organized religion. The region was first settled around 10,000 BC.
Facts to Know

Mesopotamian metalworkers learned to make bronze by mixing copper and tin. Metal was smelted at extremely high temperature and was poured into the moulds to create various items such as tools, weapons, and sculptures.
The Sumerian Civilization

The Sumerain civilization is the world's oldest known ancient civilization that flourished 6000 years ago in the Fertile Crescent of Mesopotamia. The heartland of Sumer developed between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. The Sumerians are regarded as the founder of civilization. Around 5000 years ago, Sumerian villages grew so large that they became cities.
The Sumerian Civilization

Sumerians were primarily farmers who constructed drains and irrigation channels to enhance agriculture. The geographical area of Sumer and the various empires that ruled Mesopotamia are depicted on the map.
Facts to Know
The name 'Sumer' is derived from Akkadian, the language of northern Mesopotamia and means 'land of civilized kings.'
System of Hierarchy

The Sumerians war leaders gained prominence and eventually became rulers. A social hierarchy was created. The ruling family, high level priests, and top officials held the highest positions in the society. The second level of hierarchy consisted of government officials and priests. The third tier included scribes, merchants and Artisans. The farmers and slaves made up the lowest rank in this hierarchy.
Discoveries and Inventions

Among the remains of Sumer, archaeologists have discovered agricultural and other tools made of stone and bronze. These include hoes, knives, adzes, as well as clay artifacts such as sickles, bricks, painted pottery and porcelains that are still in use today. The earliest form of writing, Cuneiform, was invented by the Sumerians.
Discoveries and Inventions
The discovery of seals demonstrates that Sumerians traded with ancient Egypt and the Indus Valley civilizations.
Status of Women in Sumerian Civilization

The Sumerian women had some degree of independence and respect. Many women performed household responsibilities whereas men were regarded as the family's head. Women enjoyed many rights in society as a result of their religious beliefs and traditions. Women served as priestesses, and some were so powerful that they could buy and sell property, slaves, run businesses and perform religious ceremonies.
Babylonian Empire

The Babylonian civilization was amongst the first empire builders who rose in ancient Mesopotamia. Babylonian cities were built along the Euphrates River. In 1792 BC, Hammurabi became the first king of Babylon.
Babylonian Empire

Under Hammurabi's rule, Babylon developed as the cradle of learning and culture and grew into a powerful city by erecting magnificent and lavish buildings, royal palaces with compounds, gardens, cemeteries, and ziggurats. In cities like Ur, residential areas were made up of ordinary houses on winding streets dotted with elite housing, shops, and shrines.
Do You Know?
A ziggurat is a pyramidal terraced temple tower that was architecturally and religiously significant in the main cities of Mesopotamia.
Hanging Gardens of Babylon

The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were regarded as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Some historians believe that Assyrian King Sennacherib built "The Hanging Gardens" in Nineveh. King Sennacherib called it 'Wonder for all people'. The garden was well-known for its fruit orchards, pine trees, rosewood, olive trees, oaks and grape vines.
Code of Hammurabi

The city states in Babylon had their own laws. The most well-known is the Hammurabi Code that consisted of written legal codes inscribed in cuneiform script on a stone tablet. The Hammurabi's code stated:
Code of Hammurabi
i. the strong should not harm the weak • ii. develop the rule of morality in the country • iii. punish the wicked and evil-doers
Code of Hammurabi

Hammurabi's Code strengthened the concept that the government was responsible to compensate the victims. After the death of Hammurabi, laws were not fairly applied to all citizens because poor people received harsher punishments than the wealthy and powerful. This was one of the major reasons for the decline of Babylonian civilization.
Ancient Egyptian Civilization

Egypt is one of the oldest countries of the world with 5000 years of recorded history. It is home to one of the world's most ancient civilizations i.e Egyptian civilization. Egypt is well-known for its Nile River, pyramids, pharaohs, inventions, historical monuments, and unique architecture.
Note for Teachers (Group Debate)
Hold a class discussion about these issues.
Note for Teachers (Group Debate)
What should be the primary goal of laws: to encourage good behaviour or to punish bad behavior? • Do all communities require a system of law to guide them?
Note for Teachers (Group Debate)
As you prepare for the discussion, consider what you've learned about the changes that occur as civilizations expand and become more advanced. Suggest why societies created legal systems.
Ancient Egyptian Civilization

Egypt is surrounded by two huge seas: the Red Sea and the Mediterranean Sea. There are deserts i.e. the Sinai and western Libyan deserts. The world's longest river Nile which flows from Africa to the Mediterranean Sea, is Egypt's life line. All round the year, the river Nile provided the Egyptians with water, fresh fish, and fertile soil.
Ancient Egyptian Civilization
All these factors contributed to the longevity of ancient Egyptian civilizations. Therefore this civilization was called "the gift of the Nile.
Early Period of Ancient Egypt

The predynastic Period of Ancient Egypt is the time between 5000 BC and 3000 BC. Many important aspects of Egyptian civilization that we know today, first appeared during this time period, such as the pyramids and the development of writing. Chronologists divide the early period into three kingdoms:
1) Old Kingdom (3000 – 2160 BC)

Memphis was Egypt's most important city at the time. During this time, the pharaohs began to construct the pyramids, which are tombs for deceased kings and queens. The famous pyramids built during this period, can still be found in Giza. Sneferu, Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure are some important pyramids.
1) Old Kingdom (3000 – 2160 BC)
In ancient Egypt, women had rights and freedom, even the ability to become pharaoh. For example Hatshepsut. She was more interested in trade which brought immense wealth to Egypt.
2) Middle Kingdom (2050 – 1170 BC)

Thebes became the most important city during the middle kingdom. This epoch is well-known for its culture and arts. The Egyptians learned how to make bronze weapons and fight their enemies with chariots.
Note for Teachers

The Egyptian civilization developed in the narrow strip of fertile land along the river Nile. Instruct the students to study the map and describe the location of the Nile River and other important landmarks.
3) New Kingdom (1550 – 1070 BC)

During this time period, Egypt became the most influential country. Ramses II of the 19th dynasty was the most powerful Egyptian pharaoh. During this time period, the Valley of the Kings was also created and believed to be the final resting place of ancient Egyptian kings and queens. Most pharaohs were men but some well-known pharaohs, such as Nefertiti and Cleopatra, were women.
Do You Know?
In 332 BC, Alexander the Great conquered Egypt and founded Alexandria as the new capital city. In 30 BC, Egypt became a Roman province after Cleopatra VII lost the battle of Actium.
Agriculture in Ancient Egyptian Civilization

Farmers in ancient Egypt were able to produce surplus food which was used during famines and droughts. Food was stored in state-owned granaries for trading. Irrigation through Shaduf was widely used. Cattle were domesticated animals together with ducks, cows, and geese. Hoes and sickles, hand ploughs, and pitchforks were among the most important tools used by Egyptian farmers.
Time to Think
Inform the students that a painting source is considered useful when it has accurate and unbiased information.
Time to Think
How useful is the source (Tomb painting) to understand the agricultural activities of ancient Egyptians?
Facts to Know
Shaduf is a hand-operated device for lifting water, invented in ancient times and still used in India, Egypt, and some other countries to irrigate land.
Facts to Know

Granaries: Since ancient times, grain has been stored in bulk. As early as 8500 BC, buildings known as granaries were used to house the cereal crops harvested by settlements. These structures were used to protect grains, such as wheat and barley, from rodents and insects.
Everyday Life of an Ancient Egyptian

In ancient Egypt, men were the heads of families, and their wives were in charge of the household and the education of the children. Men had more rights than women in most other early civilizations. Egyptian women could own and pass on property. Some women had their own businesses. Egyptians used to wear loose white linen clothing due to hot climate.
Everyday Life of an Ancient Egyptian
The common man was very interested in hunting, fighting games, races, and battles. Egyptians loved music and played harps, flutes, and drums.
Egyptian Craftsman
The craftsmen in ancient Egypt were usually trained and skilled laborers. They had fine tools made of copper and bronze.
Writing

Writing first appeared in Egypt around 3000 BC on temple walls and in pyramids. Hieroglyphics was the name given by the Greek people to the earliest Egyptian writing. It made use of both images and abstract forms. The hieratic script is a simplified version of hieroglyphics. This was used in both business and everyday life. In seminaries, Egyptian scribes taught the art of writing.
What were Hieroglyphics?

Egyptians used Papyrus rolls as writing papers. Like Mesopotamians, Egyptians also developed their own system of writing called hieroglyphics. Originally it was made up by combining the symbols of sounds and pictures which stood for objects and ideas.
Religion

The ancient Egyptians created a religion based on gods and goddesses. They believed that their deities or goddesses were in charge of their lives. Animals such as lions, cats and crocodiles were frequently used to represent their gods.
The Mummies

The ancient Egyptians believed in the concept of afterlife. This was the primary reason for the ancient ritual of mummification. The body was cloth-wrapped and adorned with jewels and charms. A mask bearing the likeness of the deceased was placed on the face. Drinks, food, and riches were buried with the mummy. In 1922, Howard Carter discovered
The Mummies
an important tomb in the Valley of the Kings. The solid gold mask that covered King Tutankhamen's mummy made this tomb famous around the world.
The Pyramids

The pyramids are the most iconic feature of ancient Egypt. Egypt has more than one hundred pyramids. The Temple of Abu Simbel, built by the later pharaoh Ramses II (1279–1213 BC), is the most famous historical monument of ancient Egypt. The Great Pyramid of Giza is declared as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
The Pyramids

According to Herodotus, an ancient Greek historian, the Great Pyramid took nearly 20 years to build. The shape of Pyramid is three dimensional. Each corner of the base is connected to the peak that forms the triangular face of a pyramid. The pyramids of Giza remain impressive monuments to this day.
Do You Know?

The pyramids are the stone tombs of Pharaohs and they are one of the world's greatest historical mysteries. They have stood for thousands of years containing many hidden secrets such as stories about Pharoahs, clues about life and death in Ancient Egypt.
Note for Teachers

Inform the students that the pyramids were added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1979, and that the organization has sponsored many missions to assess the status of these pyramids since 1990. Conduct a whole class discussion to learn why the pyramids were built and how they still affect us today.
Governance and Society in Ancient Egypt

Egyptian society was organized like a pyramid. The pharaohs were at the top. Pharaohs were the kings and queens of Egypt. Next to him was Vizier. All the other officials reported to the vizier. Other officials who reported to Pharaoh were the priests, army commanders, the chief treasurer, and the minister of public works. Scribes kept track of the finances and recorded taxes and the census.
Governance and Society in Ancient Egypt

The farmers who lived in small villages always paid the taxes on the crops they grew. This strata of society also provided soldiers in the military and forced labor for building projects in the kingdom.
Duties of Pharaoh
Pharaoh's responsibilities included:
Duties of Pharaoh
(i) keeping Egypt united • (ii) leading in good and bad times • (iii) issuing orders • (iv) participation in religious ceremonies
Developing and Supporting Opinions

Historians form opinions about the past as they interpret it and assess the significance of historical events and people. They back up their opinion with logical thinking, facts, examples, quotes and event references.
Developing and Supporting Opinions
Ask students to develop their opinion by answering the question why Paharohs were always powerful in ancient Egypt. Summarize your opinion and supporting information in a chart provided.

The study of previous events through inquiry, narratives, and recorded documents is known as history. History helps in the comprehension of global issues. • River valleys were the birthplace of all early civilizations. Mesopotamian civilizations influenced the evolution of human civilization by inventing irrigation and sailboats. • The class system was popular in Sumerian civilization.
What I have learned

Some Sumerian women were wealthy and powerful priestesses. • Hammurabi was a Babylonian monarch who codified his kingdom's laws. • The Nile River, pyramids, pharaohs, innovations, and historical sites are famous in Egyptian Civilization.

introduce Chinese civilization and describe the main features of the Shang and Zhou dynasties. • describe the early settlements in Mehergarh. • explain the importance of Indus River in the establishment of huge settlements (Mohenjodaro and Harappa) of Indus Valley Civilization.

Chinese Civilization

China has one of the oldest civilizations on this planet. It has a 6000 year old history. China is separated from the rest of the world by high mountains, deserts, dense jungles, and the vast Pacific Ocean. The Huang Ye valley, where Neolithic people learned to farm, is where Chinese history began.
The Shang and Zhou Dynasties

The Xia dynasty ruled most of Northern China for approximately 1100 years (2700 – 1600 BC) under Emperor Jie, who was known for his tyranny. Tang, a Shang leader, defeated Jie in a great battle around 1650 BC. The Shang dynasty ruled for nearly 554 years (1600-1046 BC). After Shangs, the Zhou emperor established the Zhou/Chou Dynasty.
The Shang and Zhou Dynasties

The Zhou dynasty was later destroyed by the Qin emperors, resulting in the formation of the Qin Dynasty (221-206 BC). Qin dynasty ruled China as a single entity and extended its control throughout the country.
Time to Think
What does the portrait tell you about King Wu? Notice the visual details, make inference and develop the underlying message.
Note for Teachers
Ask the students to describe the information provided by the map about Chinese civilizations.
Shang and Zhou Governance and Religion

Shang Dynasty was ruled by absolute monarchs whereas the Zhou emperor ruled the dynasty by feudal system. The king was the only authority to make laws in the country, and no one else had the power to dominate him. In ancient Shang and Zhou dynasties, society was organized through social hierarchy.
Do You Know?
The organization of social groups into a hierarchy strengthen the society because it is an efficient way to divide goods and services among people having varying individual skills.
Religion

In ancient China, people had a wide range of religious beliefs. They adhered to a polytheistic religion and believed in spirits. Shangs thought that worshipping the spirits of their forefathers would bring blessings and good fortune to their families.
Economy

During the Shang and Zhou eras, the empire's economy was mainly based on agriculture. Historians note that the presence of fertile alluvial sediment on either side of Yellow river enabled Shang and Zhou people to grow more food. Wealth and skilled labor were available for other innovative works such as Shang tombs, walled cities and the Grand Canal.
Chinese Village
Chinese farmers lived in small villages made up of several families. They farmed fields outside the village walls.
Chinese Village

Villagers built walls that surrounded and protected the town. • Since horses were more valubale as war animals, farmers used oxen and water buffalo to pull plows and carts. • Foot-pedaled hammers were used to remove grain and rice from their stalks. • Peasants planted and cultivated rice plants in large flooded fields.
Discoveries and Inventions

During the Shang and Zhou periods, the Chinese studied the movement of the planets, recorded eclipses, and developed an accurate calendar. As China's Bronze Age reached its peak, the Shang Dynasty produced writing system, exquisite bronze vessels, horse-drawn Chariot and weapons.
Note for Teachers
Ask the students to search on the internet and find countries that use chopsticks as eating utensils.
Ethical Code of Confucius

Confucius was a Chinese philosopher who flourished around 500 BC. His teachings had a significant impact on the development of Chinese character, behaviour, and way of life. He taught appropriate personal behaviour and advised that children should respect their elders. He hilighted that a good leader should have a strong moral character and serve as a role model for his people.
Ethical Code of Confucius

Confucius believed that the ideals of justice, respect, love, wisdom and sincerity are at the heart of good governance. The Confucius Code of Ethical Life is a compilation of lessons that are still relevant in modern China.
Saying of Confucius
Confucius is famous for many of his sayings which guide us how to learn best: I hear and I forget, I see and I remember, I do and I understand.
Mehrgarh Civilization

Pakistan's history reveals that it has been home to some of the world's earliest civilizations. Mehrgarh, Mohenjo-Daro, Harappa, Taxila have all been recognized as important archaeological sites around the world. Mehrgarh is thought to be the forerunner of the Indus Valley Civilization.
Mehrgarh Civilization
Between 7000 and 5500 BC, Mehrgarh was a small pre-Indus farming and pastoral settlement located at the foot of the Bolan Pass in Balochistan, Pakistan.
Note for Teachers (Whole class discussion)
Is Confucius more concerned with personal behaviour or in behaviour towards others? Explain your choice.
Note for Teachers (Whole class discussion)
Ask the students to describe the location of the civilization of Mehrgarh shown on the map of Pakistan.
Time to Think
Observe the visuals details of the picture and describe the impression it gives of Mehrgarh civilization.
Mehrgarh Civilization

During the excavation, a large number of items were discovered, including figurines, polychrome pottery, bronze shaft-hole axe, beads, and seals, demonstrating the presence of a highly developed society. The presence of cotton seeds suggests the use of fiber for textile production.
Mehrgarh Civilization
The Mehrgarians' remnants can still be seen at Balochistan's Sibi cattle exhibition and the turban worn by the inhabitants of Balochistan.
Pottrey and Bead Making at Mehrgarh

Jean-Francois Jarrige (1940-2014) and his wife Catherine (1942) were two of the most well-known archaeologists in South Asia, whose excavations at Mehrgarh were very important. According to their research, Mehrgarians used a variety of specific artisan techniques. Pottery and necklaces with glazed steatite beads were among the items discovered during the graveyard dig.
Note for Teachers

Mehergarh is a testimony to the idea that the Indus Civilization was founded by Mehrgarian, not foreigners. Harappa-Mohenjo-Daro's urban civilization is not the outcome of an accident. The Harappan civilization is a wonderful example of the growth of human civilization in and around Mehrgarh.
Indus Valley Civilization

The Indus Valley Civilization rose along the Indus River and its tributaries. The Indus Valley stretches from modern-day northeast Afghanistan to Pakistan, and northwest of India. Harappa in Punjab and Mohenjo Daro in Sindh were the two major towns of the Indus Valley. The Indus Valley was fertile, and that allowed large-scale farming. Agriculture and trade were the main sources of their economy.
Indus Valley Civilization
The farmers grew crops such as cotton, wheat, barley, peas and fruits. In trade, the river Indus facilitated the ease of shipment.
Governance and Law

The remains of Mohenjo Daro and Harappa suggest that the governance in Indus Valley was founded on religion and trade with commands coming from great priests or Monarchs. The Indus Valley Civilization had laws to care for nature, to avoid violence, and to pay taxes. One of the laws was that women should be treated with respect.
Religion and Writing Script

Polytheism was widespread in the Indus Valley. Many stamps and seals with depictions of animals and humans were discovered during the excavations. Archeologists found the earliest known examples of the Indus script used during the early Harappan phase, but it could not be translated into other languages.
Time to Think
Take a close look at the seals and writings. What can we learn about the civilization from the animal engravings? Express your views.
Note for Teachers (Pair discussion)
How close is your city to Mohenjo Daro and Harappa? You may mention your province or city to compare the location.
Note for Teachers (Pair discussion)

Explain to the students that the Indus Valley Civilization is also known as the Harappan Civilization since Harappa was the first city discovered by archaeologists. Mohenjo Daro is the Indus Valley civilization's largest metropolis. It was discovered in 1922. In 1980, Mohenjo Daro was declared as UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Town Planning

The Indus Valley Civilization consisted of mostly urban areas where people lived a highly civilized life. This means that it had proper and well-planned cities. Interestingly, many of the features are still present in modern day Pakistan.
Town Planning

The houses were made up of sun-dried bricks. Streets were fairly wide having a width between 10-30 feet. Beneath the streets were many small drains that carried waste and sewerage towards the major drains out of the city. There were two very important buildings found in the Indus Valley, the granary and a public bath.
Town Planning
The public bath was a huge area on a mound present in the center of the city. It was covered with tar and clay so that water would stay in it.

The Persian Empire

The Persian Empire (6th Century BC to 20th Century AD) was a series of dynasties centered in modern-day Iran and was considered as one of the benevolent empire of the world. It is worth noting that Alexander the Great chose the same path to conquer the Achaemenid dynasty a century and a half later.

By 1700 BCE, Indus Valley Civilization faded and Indian history entered a new stage. During this time of collapse, India saw waves of Aryans migration from the Northwest mountains.

Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded by his son Bindusara who ruled from 297 BCE until his death in 272 BCE. After him the throne was taken over by his son Ashoka who became the most powerful ruler of the Mauryan dynasty.

Historians use the skill of synthesizing to develop interpretations of historical events. Synthesizing includes the act of putting clues, information, and ideas together to form an overall picture of a historical event. The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka (304 BC-232 BC)

Ashoka was one of the greatest emperors of the Mauryan Empire. During eighth year of his reign, he took the empire to its glory through his geographical expansions. He was ambitious and fiercely aggressive throughout his early reign as a monarch. He expanded the Mauryan Empire even further, ruling almost the whole Indian Subcontinent from modern-day Afghanistan to Bangladesh in the East.
The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka (304 BC-232 BC)
The wide spread bloodshed and barbaric nature of the conquest stirred the human nerve in Ashoka. He left armed conquest and adopted a policy called "conquest by religion".
The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka (304 BC-232 BC)

His inclination to Buddhist ideals of tolerance, non-violence, and good behaviour towards all people eventually led him to embrace Buddhism. It was due to Ashoka that Buddhism spread beyond the frontiers of the empire. Ashoka sent missionaries to Southeast Asia to preach Buddhism.
Achievements of Ashoka

After his spiritual transformation, Ashoka's administration was mainly focused on the well-being and prosperity of his subjects. The direct collection of taxes on agriculture and provision of justice to the people were the two main pillars of his government.
Achievements of Ashoka
He showed his non-violent outlook of life through the edicts or laws carved onto the stones or the pillars of the famous trade routes and the pilgrimage sites in the empire.

Many historians consider Ashoka to be the first ruler in written history to push for wildlife conservation. He practiced non-violence, by abstaining from royal hunting and animal sacrifices. Kushan Empire

The Kushans were a nomadic tribe who descended from the Yuezhi; they migrated from Northern China (Xinjiang and Gansu) to ancient Bactria. The Yuezhi conquered Bactria in the 2nd century BCE. A hundred years later the Kushan chief Kujula Kadphises secured the political unification of the Yuezhi kingdom under himself.
Kushan Empire
The Kushan Empire was a nomadic civilization in Asia and it was largely influenced by Greece, Iran, and India due to its strategic location at a cultural crossroads.
Great King of Kushan Empire

Kanishka is recognized as the greatest emperor of Kushan Empire. He was the third emperor of the Kushan dynasty succeeding Kujula Kadphises and Vima Kadphises. Kanishka's empire extended from present-day Bihar to the Indus Valley in the west. Puruspur, near modern-day Peshawar, stood as the empire's capital. He was acclaimed for his exploits in the military and politics.
Great King of Kushan Empire
Kanishka was the follower of Buddhism and thus promoted its teachings in his empire.
Great King of Kushan Empire

Kanishka and his successors expanded the Kushan Empire to the fourth greatest Eurasian power after China, Rome, and Parthia. Kanishka was also responsible for spreading Sanskrit throughout the region. During his reign, the Roman and Chinese empires had friendly connections with the Kushan Empire. Kanishka established the Gandhara School of Arts, a unique mix of western and eastern ideas.
Great King of Kushan Empire

Furthermore, links with the Roman Empire via the Silk Road facilitated the flow of commodities as well as ideas. His conquests and support of Buddhism were important to the Silk Road's development and the spread of Mahayana Buddhism from Gandhara to China over the Karakoram range.

Buddhism made its initial appearance in China in the 2nd century CE.
Art and Culture

Kushan relics display imperial art of Iranian origin and also Buddhist art with a blend of Greco-Roman and Indian influences. Buddha sculptures display the beliefs and arts of the Kushan Dynasty as evident from different coins. Kushans followed Zoroastrianism, Greek cults and Buddhism.
Ajanta and Ellora

Ajanta and Ellora are renowned masterpieces of Buddhist religious art and have had a significant impact on India's art history. The Ajanta and Ellora caves are carved into the mountains. Both are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Ajanta and Ellora

Ellora has 34 caves dating from the 6th to 11th centuries AD, whereas Ajanta has 29 caves spanning from the 2nd century BC to the 6th century AD. Ajanta's caves are all Buddhist, but Ellora's caves are a mix of Buddhist, Hindu, and Jain caves. The Ajanta Caves are carved into a 75-meter (246-foot) rock wall. These caves contain ancient monasteries and worship halls of several Buddhist schools.
Ajanta and Ellora

According to the ancient Indian texts, Ellora Caves were used as a monks' monsoon retreat and a resting place for merchants and pilgrims. Various emperors contributed funds to the construction of the caves. The rock-cut sculptures, murals and paintings in Ajanta Caves are generally themed around Buddhism and Jainism. Ellora caves are located nearly 100 km away from Ajanta caves.
Facts to Know

Ajanta and Ellora caves were built to honor the glory of Gautama Buddha's life and achievements, but they also give useful insight into Buddhist life and belief systems as well as artistic reflection of their values.
Gupta Empire (320 CE- 550 CE)

In the second decade of the 4th century CE, a new power emerged in India called the Gupta. The Gupta reunited India after the decline of Kushan Empire. The Gupta Empire was mainly based in northern India with some parts of central and southern India. They ruled from nearly 320-550 CE. This period is famous for its remarkable contributions to science, administration, architecture and philosophy.
Gupta Empire (320 CE- 550 CE)

Chandragupta I is considered to be the real founder of the Gupta Empire. He started conquering the neighboring states and soon established himself as the first sovereign ruler of the empire. Prominent rulers of this dynasty were Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II and Skandagupta.
The Golden Period of India

Historians call Gupta reign as the golden period of Indian history due its achievements in empire consolidation and socio-economic fields. Among other achievements, the period is marked by economic prosperity and stable governance. Food was in abundant, trade and industries flourished. People were prosperous and had a high standard of living.
The Golden Period of India
In this period, numerous achievements were made in the fields of science, technology, engineering, astronomy, religion and philosophy.
Cultural Development

This period was also remarkable in terms of cultural development. The Gupta dynasty rulers took great interest and supported cultural development initiatives. During this period, considerable progress was achieved in the fields of art, architecture, sculpture, literature and painting. The Sanskrit language flourished and was patronized.
Cultural Development

In poetry, prose, drama and grammar, several marvelous literary pieces were produced. Kalidasa was the most prominent poet and dramatist of Gupta's period. He wrote some famous dramas which are still popular in India.

Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was a wealthy businessman and a respected citizen of Makkah even before embracing Islam. He was three years younger than Hazrat Muhammad Rasulullah Khatam un Nabiyeen (ﷺ) and known to him since childhood. He remained the closest companion of the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) throughout his life.
Caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (رضی اللہ عنہ) (632-634 AD)

When the Holy Prophet (ﷺ) first invited the people to Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was among the earliest to accept it. Later, Holy Prophet (ﷺ), gave him the title of 'Siddiq' - 'The Testifier to the Truth.'
Governance and Administration

Caliphate period of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (رضی اللہ عنہ) was short but very important. On the footprints of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم), Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) led the community as an exemplary leader.
Governance and Administration
On his appointment as Caliph, he said these historical words:
First address of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ)

*"I am appointed as Leader upon you but I am not better than you. If I do well, help me and if I go wrong, correct me. Obey me if I obey Allah and His messenger but if I disobey them, you need not to obey me."*
Governance and Administration
These words depict manifesto of his government.
Governance and Administration

Simple Living: As a Caliph of the Islamic state, he lived a simple life and was always accessible to his people. On his death bed, Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) enquired his family members about how much of his possessions increased during his caliphate period. Upon learning that it was increased by a camel, a slave and a velvet sheet, he ordered handing them over to the next Caliph.
Governance and Administration
When the next caliph Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) received these items, he cried and said "You have made life difficult for successors."
Governance and Administration

Humble but Firm: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (رضی اللہ عنہ) was normally very sympathetic and kind towards his people but he also stood firm when some tribes refused to pay Zakat and did not accept the authority of the Caliph. Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) not only disciplined those tribes but also used their support against the powerful empires of the East:
Governance and Administration
the Sasanians in Persia and the Byzantines in Syria, Palestine, and Egypt.
Dealing with the Problem of False Prophets

Another issue during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was claims of false prophethood. One such claimant was Musaylima al-Kazzab. An army was sent under the command of Hazrat Khalid Bin Waleed (رضی اللہ عنہ). After many battles, Muslims got victory and Musaylima was killed.
Dealing with the Problem of False Prophets

Administrative Measures: During the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ), the country was divided into different provinces for local administration, headed by governors. Arabia was divided into ten provinces, Iraq was divided into three provinces while Syria was divided into four provinces.
Dealing with the Problem of False Prophets
The duties of governor included leading prayers, supervising the army, tax collection, maintenance of law and order and social services.
Dealing with the Problem of False Prophets
For collection of revenue, Aamils were appointed. The minorities were given complete security of life and freedom of religion.
Social Values and Justice

Humble Nature: Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) lived in an ordinary house. Any person could approach him easily in case of any issue. He always took quick actions to solve the issues of the people. Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) himself led the prayers and took the people in confidence in formulating his policies.
Social Values and Justice
Equality: Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was a great advocate of equality. For him, all people, rich or poor, high or low were equal.
Social Values and Justice
Justice: Caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was also a symbol of justice. In order to
Social Values and Justice
administer justice, Qazis were appointed. In the court of Qazi everyone was equal.
Social Values and Justice

Compilation of Quran: Another contribution of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was the collection and compilation of the verses of the Quran into a single copy. This act benefited the Muslim community a great deal.
Social Values and Justice

Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (رضی اللہ عنہ) died on 23 August 634 A.D. at the age of sixty-three, and was buried by the side of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم). The period of caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) was very short. During this short time, he strengthened and consolidated the community.
Social Values and Justice
Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) proposed the name of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) as his successor Caliph, which was accepted by the leading companions.
Caliphate of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) (634-644 AD)
Just like Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) too, after assuming the responsibility of caliph in 634 AD, addressed the community in an inspirational manner:
First address of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ)

*"O people, remain conscious of Allah, forgive me my faults and help me in my task. Assist me in enforcing what is good and forbidding what is evil. Advise me regarding the obligations that have been imposed upon me by Allah..."*
Caliphate of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) (634-644 AD)

Hazrat Umar Bin Khattab (رضی اللہ عنہ) was born into a respected Quraish family thirteen years after the birth of Hazrat Muhammad Rasulullah Khatam un Nabiyeen (ﷺ). Following the example of Holy Prophet (ﷺ) and continuing the legacy of Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ), Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) led the community in the most befitting manner.
Caliphate of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) (634-644 AD)

Before assuming caliphate, Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was a trader but after accepting responsibility of the caliph, he accepted a modest allowance. Later, when the leading companions realized that the amount was not enough for his needs, they thought of raising this allowance.
Caliphate of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) (634-644 AD)

Listening to this, Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) got angry and reminded his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (رضی اللہ عنہا) (who brought the message) the life style of the Holy Prophet (ﷺ). He spent very simple and graceful life.
Caliphate of Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) (634-644 AD)

Caliphate of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was a great symbol of justice and equality. For a larger community, he solved various problems for both Muslims and the Non-Muslims. The most notable feature of the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was the massive expansion of Islam. Apart from Arabia, Iraq, Palestine, Egypt and Iran also came under the safety of the Islamic State.
Note for Teachers

Inform the students that, Hazrat Abu Bakr (رضی اللہ عنہ) accompanied Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) in migration to Madinah Munawwara. Remind the students about the event of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) embracing Islam. Inform that his embracing Islam provided great power to the Muslim community.
Governance and Administration

Justice and Equality: Hazrat Umar Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) was an expert Islamic jurist, known for his just nature. It was this quality that earned him the title Al-Farooq. His governance is considered climax of Muslim management and rule in the world.
Governance and Administration

Innovator of Bureaucracy: Hazrat Umer Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) was an innovator of bureaucracy and governance. He ordered to keep the records of officials and soldiers. He also held a record system of the messages he sent to Governors and heads of states. He initiated the police system to maintain civil order. Hazrat Umer Farooq (رضی اللہ عنہ) initiated many projects for the welfare of people.
Governance and Administration
Stipends were given to feeding mothers and elderly people.
Governance and Administration

State Administration: To maintain good governance, the state was divided into eight or more provinces headed by governors. Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) chose his governors carefully, ensuring that they would be easily accessible to common people. Those governors had to take oath that they would not adopt lavish lifestyle and serve the people in the best possible way.
Governance and Administration
The provinces were further divided into districts for better administration.
Do You Know?
During the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) office bearers were:
Do You Know?

Katib, or Chief Secretary; • Katib-ud-Diwan or Secretary, • Sahib-ul-Kharaj or Revenue Collector; • Sahib-ul-Ahdath or Police Officer; • Sahib-ul-Bait-ul-Mal or Treasury Officer • Qazi, the Chief Judge
Governance and Administration

In order to enhance the efficiency, the officers were given handsome salary. At the time of their appointment, a list of their possessions was prepared and kept in record. If there was an unusual increase in the possessions of that officer, he was immediately called to account.
Governance and Administration

The caliphate of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) is also known for his respect for the social values. Construction of canals, introduction of a system of collecting direct information concerning the State, digging of wells, building of houses, and fixing a daily payment for the destitute among the Christians and the Jews are few of his revolutionary steps.
Do You Know?
Among the pious caliphs, most of the conquests happened during the reign of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ). This includes the conquest of Jerusalem.
Governance and Administration

Welfare of People: As a Caliph, Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was always concerned about the welfare of his people. He used to go around in disguise, in the city of Madinah at night, to see if anyone was in need of help. Once, he observed a woman cooking something in a pot
Note for Teachers
Discuss with the students that how good governance may be ensured through action of assets declaration.
Governance and Administration

while her children were crying around her. He found out from woman that the children had been hungry for two days and that the pot was put on fire just to console them. He immediately brought all the necessary food items to the woman himself.
Governance and Administration

Fear of Allah: He always had fear of Allah and love for the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) in his heart. He never used even oil from the Bait-ul-Mal to burn a lamp at night for his personal needs. Whenever he finished the official work, he put off the lamp.
Do You Know?

On one occasion when he was suggested to nominate his son as a governor, Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) got very angry and rejected the proposal saying that he did not want to expose himself to criticism of appointing his own family members on high posts.
Governance and Administration

Symbol of Justice: Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was the symbol of justice in the Islamic History. In his caliphate, all the citizens were equal before law. Once when he appeared before a court at Madinah, the Qazi (Judge) wanted to stand in his honour, but he did not allow him to do so. He did not want any distinction between him and an ordinary person before law.
Facts to Remember
Caliph had no right and power to forgive those who were convicted by the courts.
Governance and Administration

In his time, courts were completely independent and free to give their verdict on any matter even if it was against the caliph. The government couldn't interfere in their decisions. There was complete supremacy and rule of law.
Governance and Administration

Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) is the role model for every Muslim. He was on the height of justice, piety and humility. Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) was stabbed by a Non-Muslim named Firoz. He died in 644 AD and was buried by the side of the Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم).
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)
Hazrat Usman Bin Affan (رضی اللہ عنہ) became third caliph of Islam after the death of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ). A council, comprising of leading companions, was appointed to select the new caliph.
Note for Teachers
Remind the students that justice is the key to success for nations. A nation without justice cannot survive long.
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)
After detailed deliberation, the name of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) was announced by Hazrat Abdul Rehman Bin Auf (رضی اللہ عنہ).
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)

Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) belonged to the Omayyad branch of the Quraish tribe. He was a wealthy man of Makkah who was famous for his generosity. This characteristic brought him the title "Ghani" which means generous.
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)

First Address: After being elected, Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) addressed the congregation. After glorifying Allah Almighty and the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم), he advised the people to do good deeds. He expressed his hope that he would do his best to serve Islam and the people.
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)
Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) followed the tradition of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) and greatly expanded the Islamic Regime in far off places.
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)

First Muslim Naval Force: Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) arranged first naval Muslim force to access far-away regions of the world. This force defeated the naval force of the Byzantine Empire which consisted of 500 ships. Conquests of Byzantine and Roman realms and winning the North African territories were other highlights of the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ).
Caliphate of Hazrat Usman Ghani (رضی اللہ عنہ) (644 - 656 AD)
Thus, he made exceptional efforts in spreading Islam to other corners of the world.
Do You Know?
The engraving on the seal-ring of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) was: 'I trust in the One Who created and completed (His creation).'
Governance and Administration

During the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) Islamic state was divided into twelve provinces. Every province was divided into districts and there were about 100 districts in the country. Each district was under the charge of an Aamil. The Qazi was responsible for judicial administration.
Governance and Administration

Confidence on Governors: In the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ), the governors enjoyed his confidence as they were allowed a great autonomy. The caliph did not interfere in their day to day administration. He also did not impose any restrictions on his governors.
Governance and Administration

In order to eliminate the problems caused by the differences in recitation, Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) ordered to make five or seven Mushaf of the Holy Quran under supervision of Hazrat Zaid Bin Sabit (رضی اللہ عنہ). Later the copies of this Mushaf were distributed in different parts of the world. That is why he is also called Jami ul Quran.
Social Values and Justice

On the footprints of the Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) was an embodiment of Islamic social values. During the caliphate of Hazrat Umsan (رضی اللہ عنہ) the characteristics of first two caliphs continued. These include impartial justice for all, mild and humane policies, striving in the path of Allah, and the expansion of Islam.
Social Values and Justice

Check on Social Evils: During the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) the Islamic state became prosperous. Since the first generation of the companions were mostly passed away, there were some changes observed in the society. Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) took strong notice of spreading social evils.
Do You Know?
Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) had a title "Zunnurain" that means holder of two lights. It was because he was married to two of the daughters of Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم).
Social Values and Justice

Changes in the Society: By the time, Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) became caliph, the society had changed a lot. The towns expanded as Bedouins from the desert started settling in the cities. This on one hand created diversity but one the other hand many tensions also started. These people from different areas insisted on their own culture and traditions which were not aligned with the Islamic culture.
Social Values and Justice
Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) had to tackle these issues skillfully.
Note for Teachers
Encourage the students to discuss that why is it important for a ruler to check the social evils in the society. What is the benefit of showing personal example?
Social Values and Justice

Rebellion: The caliphate of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ) lasted for twelve years. During the last six years of his caliphate a rebellion arose. Taking advantage of dissatisfaction among the people, some groups of society started conspiracies against Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ). For a ruler of vast territories, it was not impossible to deal with these rebels.
Social Values and Justice
He could have crushed the rebellion at the beginning but he did not want to shed the Muslims blood. He tried to persuade them with kindness and generosity.
Martyrdom of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ)

Unfortunately, chaos continued and a time came when his house was sieged and he was martyred while reciting Holy Quran on the afternoon of Friday, 18th Zil Hajj, 35 A.H. (June 656 A.D.). At the time of death, he was eighty-two years old.
Caliphate of Hazrat Ali Bin Abi Talib (رضی اللہ عنہ) (656 - 661 AD)

After martyrdom of Hazrat Usman (رضی اللہ عنہ), there was a situation of complete anarchy in Madinah. In such circumstances, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) became fourth Caliph of Islam. It was indeed a delicate time in the Muslim history.
Caliphate of Hazrat Ali Bin Abi Talib (رضی اللہ عنہ) (656 - 661 AD)
In his inaugural address to the congregation of the Muslims, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) said:
Inaugural address of Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ)

*"O Muslims! You have given me your pledge of loyalty, and I know that you have not done so without forethought. I want to mobilize you for obedience and service to Allah. I shall not transgress the bounds of the Book of Allah for anything. I shall promulgate the Laws of Allah which are enshrined in His Book......"*
Do You Know?
Due to his bravery, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was given the title of "Asadullah" which means "Lion of Allah".
Caliphate of Hazrat Ali Bin Abi Talib (رضی اللہ عنہ) (656 - 661 AD)

Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was the first cousin of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم). He had grown up in the Holy Prophet's own household and later married his beloved daughter, Hazrat Fatima (رضی اللہ عنہا).
Caliphate of Hazrat Ali Bin Abi Talib (رضی اللہ عنہ) (656 - 661 AD)

He remained in closest association with the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) for about thirty years. After Hazrat Khadija (رضی اللہ عنہا), Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was the first one to accept Islam.
Caliphate of Hazrat Ali Bin Abi Talib (رضی اللہ عنہ) (656 - 661 AD)

Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) learned the skill to handle difficult situations. He gained great knowledge but lived very simple life. The ideal guardianship of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) gave him such abilities that helped him exercise good governance and administration of the state.
Governance and Administration

Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) followed the government and administration pattern of Hazrat Umar (رضی اللہ عنہ) and did not make any significant changes to that. He was especially concerned about the moral standards of his governors and other officers. He never allowed them to behave inappropriately.
Governance and Administration

Once, when he got information about a governor that he was spending more time in hunting and other such recreational activities, he dismissed him. In case of any information regarding negligence of his officers, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) would write warning letters to them and take actions if necessary.
Time to Think
What is the benefit of showing sensitivity towards Public Money?
Governance and Administration

Sensitivity Regarding Public Money: Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was also very strict about public revenue and its administration. He never let any of his family members to get something more than what they deserved. Once he wrote to one of his revenue officers: "The one who embezzles the trust cannot be saved from punishment of Allah. He destroys his both worldly as well as interest of hereafter."
Governance and Administration

Military Reforms: Being an experienced army commander, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) paid special attention to armed forces. He established number of new barracks and fortresses. Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was aware of his duties as a caliph towards propagation of Islam.
Social Values and Justice

In his inaugural address to the Muslims, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) said: "O Muslims! I call upon you to assist me in my program of reconstruction. I shall not rest until I have destroyed injustice. I shall not transgress the bounds of the Book of Allah for anything. I will not be partial to anyone whoever he may be. In my sight, all of you are equal."
Social Values and Justice
His will for reliving the true essence of Islam was clear through his actions. His strict stance
Social Values and Justice
against nepotism is a proof of his sensitivity towards the social values of Islam. He gave grants to the needy and the poor from public treasury.
Social Values and Justice

Justice: When it comes to justice of Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ), it was equal for everyone, Muslim or Non-Muslim, the rich or the poor. He himself appeared before the judge regarding a case, and even the decision was given against him because of lack of evidence.
Social Values and Justice

Behaviour towards Non-Muslims: He was also very kind towards the Non-Muslims. He always asked his officers to treat them with care. Once when a canal belonging to non-Muslims was blocked, Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) wrote to his officers to get it cleaned quickly. This and many such incidents became reason for many non-Muslims to embrace Islam.
Social Values and Justice

Efforts for Unity of Ummah: Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) made all possible efforts to reunite the Muslims. He was a great scholar and the greatest jurist of his time. This was mainly because he spent a great time in the company of the Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم). Hazrat Ali faced all the difficulties of his time with great courage and determination.
Social Values and Justice

But unfortunately, the enemies of Islam, especially the hypocrites were always busy in creating differences among the Muslims. In these circumstances there were a couple of fierce battles fought among Muslims.
Social Values and Justice
Martyrdom: On 19th Ramazan, 40th Hijri Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ) was offering Namaz in the mosque of Kufa, when a Khariji, Ibne Maljam struck him with a poisoned sword on his head. After
Social Values and Justice
two days, he passed away on 21st Ramazan. With the martyrdom of Hazrat Ali (رضی اللہ عنہ), the first golden period of Islamic history came to an end.
Pious Caliphs and Essence of Muslim State

It was blessing of Allah for Islam that the first successors of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) were men of great knowledge, bravery and virtuous character. During this period, it had been the Holy Quran and the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) which guided the leaders and the people of the Islamic state.
Pious Caliphs and Essence of Muslim State
The first four pious caliphs of Islam set such standards which could not find any parallel till now.
Pious Caliphs and Essence of Muslim State

Quran and Sunnah: During the period of pious caliphate, for all four caliphs, guiding force behind government and administration was but Holy Quran and the Sunnah of Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم).
Pious Caliphs and Essence of Muslim State

Consultation: Consultation (*Shura*) was another strength behind the actions of the Caliphs. During all this period, the distinctive features of the Islamic state like justice, equality and welfare were seen in best way.
Pious Caliphs and Essence of Muslim State
These minarets of light will remain as the best examples to follow for the rulers till the end of time.
What I have learned

Before Islam, the social, economic, and political conditions of Arabs were very poor. • Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) changed the conditions of the Arabs. He established the first Muslim state in Madinah, which is a model to be followed till the end of time. • The Constitution of Madinah is an example of finding solution to the problems in a peaceful manner.
What I have learned

• During the ten years that Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) lived in Madinah Munawwara, the city became a center for political, cultural, and religious enthusiasm. • Islam's message of equality, women rights, justice, system of Zakat and ideal leadership of Rasulullah (صلی اللہ علیہ وعلیٰ آلہٖ واصحابہٖ وسلم) were the main factors that changed the Arabian society.
What I have learned
• The pious caliphs of Islam set such standards which could not find any parallel till now.

متعدی امراض وہ ہیں جو کسی مریض سے تندرست شخص کو لگ جائیں۔ ان امراض کے جراثیم متاثرہ شخص یعنی مریض سے صحت مند انسان کو ہوا، پانی، غذا، لباس اور کیڑے مکوڑوں وغیرہ کے ذریعے منتقل ہوتے ہیں۔ چند متعدی امراض کے نام ذیل میں درج ہیں۔
متعدی امراض کی تعریف
نزلہ، زکام، انفلوئنزا، پیچش، تپِ دِق، تپِ محرقہ، چیچک، خسرہ، خُناق، زرد بخار اور طاعون وغیرہ۔
متعدی امراض پھیلنے کے ذرائع مندرجہ ذیل ہیں
۱۔ مریض کے کپڑے پہننے سے۔ • ۲۔ مریض کا بچا ہوا کھانا کھانے سے۔ • ۳۔ مریض کا تولیہ یا دیگر اشیا استعمال کرنے سے۔ • ۴۔ براہِ راست میل ملاپ سے۔
پرہیز
متعدی امراض ایک مریض سے تندرست انسان کو مندرجہ بالا ذرائع سے منتقل ہوتے ہیں۔ لہٰذا ان سے پرہیز کرنا ضروری ہے۔ مریض کے کھانے اور دیگر استعمال کی چیزیں الگ کرنی چاہئیں۔
غیر متعدی امراض کی تعریف

غیر متعدی امراض وہ ہیں جو ایک انسان سے دوسرے انسان کو بذریعہ ہوا، پانی، لباس یا عام میل جول سے منتقل نہیں ہوتیں بلکہ مریض کے استعمال شدہ سرنج، بلیڈ یا انتقالِ خون کے ذریعے صحت مند انسانوں کو منتقل ہوتی ہیں۔ مثلاً ہیپاٹائٹس اے، بی، سی (A, B, C)، ایڈز (AIDS) وغیرہ۔
غیر متعدی امراض کے ذرائع

ان امراض کے جراثیم زیادہ نہیں پھیلتے بلکہ جس مریض میں ہوتے ہیں اس میں ہی رہتے ہیں اور ان کا علاج بہت مشکل اور مہنگا ہوتا ہے۔ یہ عام ذرائع سے ایک بیمار شخص سے دوسروں کو نہیں لگتیں تاہم درج ذیل ذرائع سے لگ سکتے ہیں۔
غیر متعدی امراض کے ذرائع
۱۔ مریض کا خون استعمال کرنے سے۔ • ۲۔ مریض کے استعمال شدہ سرنج اور بلیڈ سے۔ • ۳۔ مریض کی استعمال شدہ سوئی سے۔ • ۴۔ گندہ پانی پینے سے۔
پرہیز

۱۔ زندگی کو اسلامی اصولوں کے مطابق گزاریں۔ • ۲۔ ذہن کو پاکیزہ اور ماحول کو صاف ستھرا رکھیں۔ • ۳۔ روزمرہ کے کاموں میں حفظانِ صحت کے اصولوں کا خیال رکھیں۔ • ۴۔ اگر خدانخواستہ کسی کو ایڈز (AIDS) یا مہلک بیماری ہو جائے تو فوراً ڈاکٹر سے رجوع کرے۔ • ۵۔ ادویات کا استعمال ڈاکٹر کی ہدایت کے مطابق کریں۔ • ۶۔ تناؤ اور ذہنی دباؤ سے بچنے کی کوشش کریں۔
یرقان (Jaundice)

انسانی جسم میں یرقان کی علامات جگر کی کارکردگی درست نہ ہونے پر ظاہر ہوتی ہیں۔ جگر ہمارے جسم کا نہایت اہم نالی دار غدہ ہے۔ یہ پسلیوں کے نیچے دائیں طرف چھاتی کے بالائی حصے میں واقع ہوتا ہے۔ اس میں خون کی بہت سی مقدار موجود ہوتی ہے۔ جگر خون کے اندر پائے جانے والے زہریلے اور فاسد مادوں کو چھان کر الگ کر دیتا ہے اور صاف و صحت مند خون کو دوبارہ دل کی طرف بھیجتا ہے۔
یرقان (Jaundice)
اس کے علاوہ جگر کے اہم افعال میں البومین (Albumin) اور خون کو جمنے میں مدد دینے والی پروٹین بنانا ہے۔
یرقان (Jaundice)

جب جگر کسی اندرونی یا بیرونی خرابی کی وجہ سے اپنا کام درست طریقے سے سرانجام نہیں دے سکتا تو یرقان کی علامات ظاہر ہونے لگتی ہیں۔ اس کیفیت میں مریض کی آنکھوں کا رنگ زرد ہو جاتا ہے جو مرض کی شدت اور نوعیت کے مطابق کم یا زیادہ ہوتا رہتا ہے۔ اگر مرض کی شدت زیادہ ہو تو آنکھوں کے ساتھ ساتھ جلد کی رنگت بھی زرد پڑ جاتی ہے اور اس کا سبب خون میں بلیروبین (Bilirubin) کی شرح نارمل سطح سے زیادہ ہو جانا ہے۔
یرقان کے اسباب
یرقان داخلی اور خارجی دونوں اسباب سے ہو سکتا ہے۔ کچھ نومولود بچوں کو پیدائش کے فوراً بعد ابتدائی دنوں میں اس کی
یرقان کے اسباب
… علامات ظاہر ہونے لگتی ہیں۔ یہ موروثی یا داخلی سبب کہلاتا ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ خارجی اسباب مندرجہ ذیل ہیں۔
یرقان کے اسباب

۱۔ آلودہ پانی کے استعمال سے۔ • ۲۔ مریض کے جسم سے نکلنے والی رطوبتوں سے۔ • ۳۔ مریض کی استعمال شدہ اشیا سے۔ • ۴۔ مریض کے استعمال شدہ بلیڈ، سرنج اور ٹوتھ برش وغیرہ سے۔ • ۵۔ مریض کے خون کے تندرست انسان میں انتقال سے۔
یرقان کی علامات
جگر کے افعال متاثر ہونے سے مریض کے جسم میں مندرجہ ذیل علامات ظاہر ہوتے ہیں۔
یرقان کی علامات

۱۔ ہلکا بخار ہوتا ہے۔ • ۲۔ آنکھوں، جلد اور ناخنوں کا رنگ زرد ہو جاتا ہے۔ • ۳۔ پیٹ میں خصوصاً جگر کے مقام پر درد محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ • ۴۔ بار بار قے آتی ہے۔ • ۵۔ بار بار پیاس کی شدت محسوس ہوتی ہے۔ • ۶۔ مریض کے پیشاب کی رنگت زرد ہوتی ہے۔
یرقان کی تشخیص
آنکھوں کی رنگت کا زرد ہونا، جگر کے مقام پر ہاتھ رکھ کر جگر کا بڑھا ہوا سائز محسوس کرنا اور مریض کے خون اور پیشاب کے نمونے کا ٹیسٹ لے کر مرض کی تشخیص کی جا سکتی ہے۔
یرقان کا علاج

نومولود بچوں میں اس مرض کا علاج نیلگوں روشنی کی شعاعوں سے کیا جاتا ہے لیکن ان شعاعوں کا استعمال ایک خاص وقت اور حد تک کیا جاتا ہے۔ اس عمل کو فوٹو تھراپی (Photo-therapy) کہتے ہیں۔ بچوں کی آنکھوں کو کپڑے سے
یرقان کا علاج

… ڈھانپ کر صبح کے وقت اور عصر کے وقت دھوپ میں رکھا جاتا ہے اور اگر ضرورت ہو تو خون میں شکر کی مقدار کو معمول پر لانے کے لیے گلوکوز کی ڈرپ بھی لگائی جا سکتی ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ مندرجہ ذیل اقدامات ضروری ہیں۔
یرقان کا علاج

۱۔ مریض کو پینے کے لیے گلوکوز ملا پانی بکثرت پلایا جائے۔ • ۲۔ جگر کی سوزش کو کم کرنے کے لیے معاون ادویات کا استعمال کیا جائے۔ یہ ادویات شربت، گولیوں اور انجکشن کی صورت میں دی جا سکتی ہیں۔ • ۳۔ مریض کو زود ہضم خوراک کا استعمال کرائیں۔ • ۴۔ مریض کو مکمل آرام کا مشورہ دیں۔
یرقان سے بچاؤ اور حفاظتی تدابیر
یرقان سے بچاؤ کے لیے مندرجہ ذیل حفاظتی تدابیر اختیار کریں۔
یرقان سے بچاؤ اور حفاظتی تدابیر

۱۔ حفظانِ صحت کے اصولوں پر عمل کیا جائے۔ • ۲۔ کھانے کی اشیا مثلاً پھل وغیرہ اچھی طرح دھو کر کھائے جائیں۔ • ۳۔ کھانے پینے کی اشیا کو مکھیوں اور جراثیم سے محفوظ رکھنے کے لیے ہمیشہ ڈھانپ کر رکھیں۔ • ۴۔ گلے سڑے پھل استعمال کرنے سے گریز کریں۔ • ۵۔ کھانا کھانے سے پہلے اچھی طرح ہاتھ دھو لیا کریں۔ • ۶۔ مریض کی استعمال شدہ اشیا مثلاً کپڑے، تولیہ اور بلیڈ وغیرہ کے استعمال سے اجتناب کریں۔ • ۷۔
یرقان سے بچاؤ اور حفاظتی تدابیر

پینے کا پانی اُبال کر استعمال کریں۔ • ۸۔ صاف اور معیاری خوراک کا استعمال کریں۔ • ۹۔ انتقالِ خون سے قبل خون کا معائنہ ضرور کریں۔ • ۱۰۔ مریض کو صاف ستھری اور ہوادار جگہ میں رکھیں اور زیادہ سے زیادہ آرام کا مشورہ دیں۔
اہم نکات
اصطلاحات اور معانی کتاب کے ہیں؛ انگریزی اور پشتو ترجمہ اسپیس بک کا ہے۔
اہم نکات

اصطلاح | مطلب; متعدی امراض | ایسے امراض جو بیمار شخص سے صحت مند شخص کو منتقل ہوتے ہیں مثلاً زکام، تپِ دق، چیچک وغیرہ۔; تشخیص | معلوم کرنا / بیماری کا پتہ لگانا; موروثی | وراثت میں ملنے والی / خاندانی; آلودہ پانی | گندہ پانی; غیر متعدی امراض | ایسے امراض جو بیمار سے صحت مند شخص کو منتقل نہیں ہوتے ہیں۔; ایڈز (AIDS) | متعدی مرض; ہیپاٹائٹس B, C | کالا یرقان; فاسد مادہ | بے کار، نقصان دہ مادہ; البومین (Albumin) | ایک قسم
اہم نکات

کا پروٹین جسے جگر بناتا ہے اور خون کو جمنے میں مدد دیتا ہے۔; بیلروبین (Bilirubin) | ایک کیمیائی مادہ جو خون میں ہوتا ہے۔; رطوبت | جسم سے نکلنے والی مائع مثلاً لعاب، پسینہ، پیشاب وغیرہ۔; یرقان | جگر کی بیماری; نومولود | بہت کم عمر بچے / پیدائش کے وقت; فوٹو تھراپی | روشنی کے ذریعے علاج کرنا; انتقالِ خون | خون دینا / کسی بیمار فرد کو دوسرے فرد کا خون منتقل کرنا۔
ہدایات برائے اساتذۂ کرام

۱۔ طلبہ کو بیمار پرسی/عیادت کے اسلامی پہلوؤں سے آگاہ کیا جائے۔ • ۲۔ احتیاطی تدابیر اختیار کرنے کی تاکید کریں۔ • ۳۔ طلبہ کو صاف ستھرا رہنے کے فوائد بتائیں۔ • ۴۔ یرقان کے مرض سے بچاؤ کی تدابیر اور مریض سے میل ملاپ کا طریقہ سمجھائیں۔
حاصلاتِ تعلّم
اس باب کی تکمیل پر طلبہ اس قابل ہو جائیں گے کہ وہ:
حاصلاتِ تعلّم

ہڈیوں کی مختلف اقسام کی نشاندہی کر سکیں اور انسانی جسم میں ان کے بنیادی افعال بیان کر سکیں۔ • پٹھوں اور اُن کی مختلف اقسام کی تعریف کر سکیں اور انسانی جسم میں ان کی بنیادی افعال بیان کر سکیں۔ • جسم کے درست اور غلط قامت (Posture) کے درمیان فرق بتا سکیں۔
ہڈیاں (Bones)
انسانی جسم میں کل 206 ہڈیاں ہوتی ہیں۔ شکل کے لحاظ سے ہڈیوں کو مندرجہ ذیل اقسام میں تقسیم کیا گیا ہے۔
لمبی ہڈیاں (Long Bones)

ان ہڈیوں کی لمبائی چوڑائی کے مقابلے میں زیادہ ہوتی ہے۔ ان ہڈیوں کے دو سرے ہوتے ہیں، درمیانی حصے کو شافٹ (Shaft) کہتے ہیں۔ یہ ہڈیاں اندر سے خالی ہوتی ہیں جن کے اندر چکنا سا مادہ موجود ہوتا ہے جس کو ہڈیوں کا گودا کہتے ہیں۔ یہ ہڈیاں ہمارے جسم میں بازوؤں اور ٹانگوں میں موجود ہوتی ہیں۔
چھوٹی ہڈیاں (Short Bones)
ان ہڈیوں کی لمبائی اور چوڑائی تقریباً یکساں ہوتی ہیں۔ ساخت کے لحاظ سے اندرونی طور پر اسفنجی جب کہ بیرونی طور پر سخت ہوتی ہیں۔ یہ ہمارے جسم میں کلائی اور ٹخنے میں موجود ہوتی ہیں۔
چپٹی ہڈیاں (Flat Bones)
ان ہڈیوں کی ساخت عموماً چپٹی ہوتی ہے۔ یہ بھی درمیان میں اسفنجی ہوتی ہیں۔ یہ ہمارے جسم میں پسلیوں، شانے اور کھوپڑی میں موجود ہوتی ہیں۔
بے قاعدہ ہڈیاں (Irregular Bones)
ان ہڈیوں میں سخت ہڈی اور اسفنجی ہڈی دونوں کی تہہ پائی جاتی ہیں۔ یہ ہڈیاں ہمارے جسم میں ریڑھ کی ہڈی کے مہروں، چہرے اور کولہے میں پائی جاتی ہیں۔
سیس موائڈ ہڈیاں (Sesmoid Bones)
یہ انتہائی چھوٹی ہڈیاں عضلات میں پائی جاتی ہیں۔ یہ ہمارے جسم میں گھٹنے کے جوڑ یعنی پٹیلا (Patella) میں موجود ہوتی ہیں۔
ہڈیوں کے کام (Functions of Bones)

۱۔ ہڈیاں انسانی جسم کی ساخت بناتی ہیں۔ • ۲۔ ہڈیوں کا ڈھانچہ تمام جسم کو سہارا دیتا ہے۔ • ۳۔ چپٹی ہڈیاں جسم کے بہت سے نازک اعضا کی حفاظت کرتی ہیں۔ مثلاً دل، دماغ اور پھیپھڑے۔ • ۴۔ ہڈیاں ایک خاص ترتیب کے ساتھ مل کر جوڑ بناتی ہیں اور ہڈیاں ان جوڑوں کے ذریعے جسم کی حرکت میں مدد دیتی ہیں۔ • ۵۔ ہڈیوں کے گودے میں خون کے سرخ ذرات پیدا ہوتے ہیں۔ • ۶۔ جسم کے عضلات ہڈیوں کے ساتھ منسلک ہو کر حرکات میں مدد دیتے ہیں۔ • ۷۔
ہڈیوں کے کام (Functions of Bones)
ہڈیاں جسم میں کیلشیم اور فاسفورس کے سٹور ہاؤس کے طور پر بھی کام کرتی ہیں۔
عضلات کی تعریف
سادہ الفاظ میں پٹھوں کو عضلات کہتے ہیں جو جلد کے نیچے ہڈیوں کے ساتھ پیوست ہوتے ہیں۔ یہ مسلسل سکڑتے اور پھیلتے ہیں جس کی وجہ سے بنیادی حرکات پیدا ہوتی ہیں۔ عضلات کی اقسام درج ذیل ہیں۔
ارادی عضلات
ارادی عضلات کی حرکات انسانی مرضی کے تابع ہوتی ہیں۔ یہ لمبے اور باریک ریشوں سے مل کر بنتے ہیں۔ یہ بازوؤں اور ٹانگوں میں پائے جاتے ہیں اور جسم کے مختلف حصوں میں موجود ہوتے ہیں۔

ایسے عضلات جن کی حرکات انسانی مرضی کے تابع نہیں ہوتے بلکہ قدرتی طور پر ان کی حرکات وقوع پذیر ہوتی ہیں۔ یہ عموماً انسان کے اندرونی نظاموں میں پائے جاتے ہیں۔ مثلاً دل، معدہ، پھیپھڑے اور نظامِ اعصاب وغیرہ۔ یہ آنکھ کی پتلی اور مثانہ میں بھی پائے جاتے ہیں۔
قلبی عضلات
یہ عضلات دل میں پائے جاتے ہیں۔ یہ کام کے لحاظ سے غیر ارادی ہوتے ہیں۔

۱۔ ارادی عضلات جسم کو حرکت کے قابل بناتے ہیں۔ • ۲۔ ہڈیوں اور جوڑوں کی حفاظت کرتے ہیں۔ • ۳۔ جسمانی نظاموں کے افعال میں مدد دیتے ہیں۔ • ۴۔ جسمانی ڈھانچہ کو قائم رکھتے ہیں۔ • ۵۔ جسم کو خوبصورت بناتے ہیں۔ • ۶۔ عضلات کے سکڑنے اور پھیلنے سے سانس لینے میں آسانی پیدا ہوتی ہے۔ • ۷۔ قامت کو درست رکھتے ہیں۔ • ۸۔ جسمانی کارکردگی کو بہتر بناتے ہیں۔ • ۹۔ مختلف سرگرمیوں مثلاً دوڑنے، چڑھنے، بیٹھنے، لیٹنے میں مدد دیتے ہیں۔ • ۱۰۔

قامت (Posture)

جسم کے مختلف حصوں کا باہم موزوں اور متناسب ہونا قامت کہلاتا ہے۔ قامت وہ بنیادی ڈھانچہ ہے جس پر کسی فرد کی متوازن شخصیت کی تعمیر کا انحصار ہوتا ہے۔ درست قامت اچھی شخصیت اور خود اعتمادی کی آئینہ دار ہوتی ہے۔ درست قامت ریڑھ کی ہڈی میں موجود فطری خم کو متوازن رکھنے سے حاصل ہوتی ہے۔ ریڑھ کی ہڈی میں اوپر کی جانب اور نیچے کی جانب قدرتی طور پر چار خم پائے جاتے ہیں۔
قامت (Posture)
ان چار خموں میں سے کسی ایک میں بگاڑ ہو تو دوسرے خم میں بھی کمی یا اضافہ کا باعث بن سکتا ہے، ایسی کیفیت قامتی نقص کا باعث بنتی ہے۔
قامت (Posture)

ریڑھ کی ہڈی کی بناوٹ مہروں سے ہوتی ہے، ان مہروں کے درمیان حفاظت کی غرض سے کُرکُری ہڈی کے چھوٹے ڈسک لگے ہوتے ہیں۔ بعض حادثات کی وجہ سے مہرے اپنی جگہ چھوڑ دیتے ہیں جس سے فطری خم میں کمی یا زیادتی ہو سکتی ہے جو قامتی نقص کا سبب بنتی ہے۔
قامت (Posture)

قامتی نقائص اکثر چھوٹی عمر میں ہی پیدا ہوتے ہیں کیونکہ چھوٹی عمر کے بچوں کی ہڈیاں نرم ہوتی ہیں۔ لہٰذا ان کے اعضا غلط اثرات جلد قبول کر لیتے ہیں۔ قامتی نقائص پیدائشی کمزوری، بیماری، زیادہ مشقت، نظر کی کمزوری، ایک یا دونوں کانوں کی سماعت کی کمزوری، چلنے پھرنے، بیٹھنے اور لیٹنے کے غلط انداز، حادثات کے نتیجے میں یا زیادہ خوراک اور متوازن غذا کی کمی کی وجہ سے ہو سکتے ہیں۔

اصطلاحات اور معانی کتاب کے ہیں؛ انگریزی اور پشتو ترجمہ اسپیس بک کا ہے۔

۱۔ طلبہ کو سکول کی سائنس لیبارٹری کا مطالعاتی دورہ کرایا جائے۔ • ۲۔ طلبہ کو چارٹ کی مدد سے نظامِ عضلات سمجھائیں۔ • ۳۔ اگر ممکن ہو سکے تو بازار سے تیار چارٹ بھی منگوائے جائیں۔
حاصلاتِ تعلّم
اس باب کی تکمیل پر طلبہ اس قابل ہو جائیں گے کہ وہ:
حاصلاتِ تعلّم
متوازن غذا کی تعریف کر سکیں۔ • جسمانی بڑھوتری اور نشوونما میں متوازن غذا کی اہمیت کو بیان کر سکیں۔
متوازن غذا کی تعریف

وہ غذا جس میں تمام بنیادی غذائی اجزاء مثلاً نشاستہ، چکنائی، پروٹین، حیاتین، نمکیات اور پانی مناسب مقدار میں موجود ہو متوازن غذا کہلاتی ہے۔ متوازن غذا زود ہضم ہوتی ہے اور کھانے کے بعد جسم کی مناسب نشوونما کرتی ہے۔ جسم کو طاقت اور توانائی مہیا کرتی ہے اور بیماریوں کے خلاف قوتِ مدافعت پیدا کرتی ہے۔
اہمیت

بچے چونکہ تیزی سے بڑھتے ہیں اس لیے انہیں ایسی غذا کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے جو بہتر نشوونما کر سکے۔ متوازن غذا کے استعمال میں جنس، عمر اور بچوں کی حرکات، کام اور کھیل کی نوعیت کو مدِنظر رکھنا ضروری ہوتا ہے۔ غذا اس تناسب سے دی جائے جس سے بچوں کی تمام جسمانی ضروریات پوری ہو سکیں۔
اہمیت

خوراک کے بنیادی اجزا اگر ضرورت سے کم یا زیادہ ہوں تو اسے متوازن غذا نہیں کہا جا سکتا۔ اسی طرح اگر تمام ضروری اجزا خوراک میں موجود نہ ہوں تو بھی وہ متوازن غذا نہیں کہلائی جا سکتی۔ جس خوراک میں تمام بنیادی اجزا مطلوبہ مقدار میں موجود نہ ہو اس سے بچوں کی جسمانی نشوونما بہتر طور پر نہیں ہو سکتی۔ ایسی صورت میں جسم کے مختلف نظام اور ان کے افعال میں مشکلات پیدا ہوتی ہیں اس لیے بچوں کی غذا کا بطورِ خاص خیال رکھنا چاہئے۔
اہمیت
جس طرح متوازن غذا نشوونما کے لیے ضروری ہے اسی طرح متوازن غذا کے اصولوں کو بھی اپنانا ضروری ہے ورنہ نشوونما کے تقاضے اور متوازن غذا کے فوائد حاصل نہیں ہوں گے۔
بہتر نتائج حاصل کرنے کے لیے درج ذیل اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھا جائے:

۱۔ غذا ملی جلی ہو۔ • ۲۔ غذا بدل کر استعمال کریں۔ • ۳۔ غذا میں مناسب وقفہ ہو۔ • ۴۔ غذا خوش ذائقہ ہو۔ • ۵۔ غذا زود ہضم ہو۔ • ۶۔ غذا ضرورت کے مطابق ہو۔ • ۷۔ غذا جنس، عمر، سرگرمیوں اور موسم کے مطابق ہو۔ • ۸۔ غذا حفظانِ صحت کے اصولوں کے مطابق ہو۔ • ۹۔ غذا کے ساتھ ساتھ ورزش، نیند اور آرام کا خیال رکھا جائے۔
بہتر نتائج حاصل کرنے کے لیے درج ذیل اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھا جائے:

اِن اُصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھتے ہوئے بچوں کو متوازن غذا دینی چاہئے۔ متوازن غذا کی بدولت جسمانی نظام بہتر کام کریں گے اور بچوں کی نشوونما میں بہتری پیدا ہوگی، بیماریوں کے خلاف قوتِ مدافعت مضبوط ہوگی، اعصاب اور عضلات میں ہم آہنگی پیدا ہوگی، بغیر تھکاوٹ کے اپنے کام اور سرگرمیاں سرانجام دے سکیں گے اور وقت پر کام، آرام اور خوراک کے عادی ہو جائیں گے۔
بہتر نتائج حاصل کرنے کے لیے درج ذیل اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھا جائے:

بچے جس قدر جسمانی طور پر مضبوط ہوں گے اسی قدر وہ ذہنی طور پر بھی صحت مند ہوں گے۔ اُن کی تعلیم میں دلچسپی بڑھے گی، پڑھائی سے رغبت پیدا ہوگی اور اُن میں صحت مندانہ عادات بھی پیدا ہوں گی۔ اگر ان اصولوں کو پسِ پشت ڈالا گیا یا اُن میں متوازن غذا کے کسی جز کی کمی رہ گئی تو بچوں کو بیماریاں لگنے کا خطرہ لاحق ہو سکتا ہے۔
بہتر نتائج حاصل کرنے کے لیے درج ذیل اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھا جائے:

اسی طرح بچے کو متوازن غذا نہ ملنے کے سبب پیٹ میں درد، چہرے کا رنگ زرد ہونا، تھکاوٹ محسوس ہونا، دانتوں کا کمزور ہونا اور قبض جیسی بیماریوں کے لگنے کا اندیشہ ہوتا ہے۔ لہٰذا بچوں کی بہتر نشوونما کے لیے ان کی غذا، آرام اور ورزش کا خیال رکھنا اہمیت کا حامل ہے۔ حفظانِ صحت کے اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھتے ہوئے بچوں کو متوازن غذا دینی چاہئے کیونکہ ایک جیسی خوراک اور بے وقت کھانا بچوں کی صحت کو خراب کر دیتا ہے۔
بہتر نتائج حاصل کرنے کے لیے درج ذیل اصولوں کو مدِنظر رکھا جائے:

اس لیے نشوونما کے مختلف مدارج کے دوران بچوں کو ضرورت کے مطابق ایسی خوراک دینی چاہئے جو کہ متوازن ہوں اور اس میں غذائیت کے لحاظ سے ضروری اجزا مناسب مقدار میں شامل ہوں۔ جن بچوں کی خوراک میں ان اصولوں کا خیال نہیں رکھا جائے گا وہ کمزور اور بیماریوں کا شکار ہو سکتے ہیں۔

بتا سکیں کہ ادویات کیوں استعمال ہوتے ہیں۔ • وضاحت کر سکیں کہ ادویات کا غلط استعمال نقصان دہ ہو سکتا ہے۔ • سکول یا گھر پر ادویات استعمال کرنے کے اصولوں کی نشاندہی کر سکیں۔
